title: WinForms Timer.Interval assigned from expression without range guard (zero / overflow / negative)
description: System.Windows.Forms.Timer.Interval expects a positive integer in milliseconds (range 1 to Int32.MaxValue). Setting Interval to 0 or a negative value throws an ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Setting it to an extremely large value effectively disables the timer silently. When interval is derived from a user/config parameter (e.g. [int]($TrayPollSec * 1000)) with no range validation, any misconfigured or zero value will crash the tray at startup. The cast to [int] can also overflow for large inputs (e.g. TrayPollSec=3600 → 3,600,000 ms which is fine, but TrayPollSec=2148 → [int] overflow). A minimum of 1ms and a sensible maximum (e.g. 300000ms = 5min) should always be enforced before assignment.
detection_method: Scan for .Interval = [int](...) or .Interval = $ patterns without [Math]::Max or -lt guard nearby
exception_message: System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException: Interval must be greater than 0.
preventionRule:
Always clamp timer interval before assignment:
  $rawMs  = [long]($TrayPollSec * 1000)
  $safeMs = [Math]::Max(1000, [Math]::Min($rawMs, 300000))
  $timer.Interval = [int]$safeMs

known_instances.risk: HIGH — TrayPollSec=0 or very large will throw on startup
